sights.w: Completed 1984, these steep red-pitched roofs are Singapore's most visually distinctive HDB silhouette — a mid-1980s experiment in postmodern public housing that borrowed the Malay kampong-house form to break from the usual slab blocks. Top-floor units get soaring 5-5.5 m ceilings, and Block 142's 'welcome' sign has become the emblem of the whole estate.
sights.k: Public estate; view from ground level

sights.address: 11 Bidadari Park Drive (opposite Woodleigh MRT), Singapore
sights.w: A 13-hectare urban park opened 3 September 2024 on the former Bidadari burial grounds, centred on Alkaff Lake — a stormwater-retention pond inspired by the colonial-era Alkaff Lake Gardens — with a 700 m Heritage Walk. Developed jointly by HDB, NParks, PUB and the National Heritage Board as the green heart of the new Bidadari estate.

Built in 1932 by Syed Abdul Rahman Alkaff of the prominent Hadhrami-Arab merchant family, this small mosque on the Potong Pasir/Bidadari edge is distinguished by a pencil-thin Ottoman-style minaret unlike any other in Singapore. Restored in 2014 and gazetted the same year as Singapore's 68th National Monument.

A 13.5-hectare Anglican mission-school complex opened in 2006, straddling the Kallang River on the Potong Pasir/Woodsville banks and linking St Andrew's Junior, Secondary and Junior College — descendants of the St Andrew's Church Mission School founded in 1862 — across the Jacob Ballas Bridge.

sights.n: Lorong Koo Chye Sheng Hong Temple
sights.w: A prominent Taoist temple near MacPherson MRT dedicated to the City God (Cheng Huang Ye), the Sheng Hong deity whose spirit was brought from Anxi, China. Rooted in the old Kampong Koo Chye, it relocated to Arumugam Road in the 1980s when the area was redeveloped for industry and is now a large temple-and-charity association drawing crowds for prosperity and good-fortune prayers.

A Hindu temple to Shiva (as Manmatha Karuneshvarar) established in 1888 on the Potong Pasir/Kallang edge, begun by Hindu workers of the nearby colonial gasworks who installed the deity for protection — hence its nickname the 'Kallang Gasworks Sivan Temple'. Rebuilt in 1934 on a 1909 government land grant.

sights.address: Jalan Wangi / Sennett Road (bounded by Upper Serangoon Rd & MacPherson Rd), Singapore
sights.w: Once dubbed Singapore's largest planned housing development, Sennett Estate was built out through the 1950s (completed 1955) by the Sennett Realty and Tan Chong Land companies on land that had been Alkaff's leisure garden in the 1920s. Today a quiet, leafy middle-class landed enclave of terraces and bungalows ringed by the Potong Pasir and MacPherson HDB towns.

sights.address: Bidadari Park (eastern section), Bidadari Park Drive, Singapore
sights.w: From 1907-1972 the Bidadari grounds were Singapore's main multi-faith cemetery — Christian, Muslim, Hindu and Sinhalese — resting place of luminaries like Lim Boon Keng. After exhumation (2001-2006) of tens of thousands of graves, its history is preserved in a memorial garden and heritage relics folded into today's Bidadari Park, an estate reborn as 'a community in a garden'.

The civic heart of the new Bidadari estate: a three-storey mall opened May 2023 (officially November 2023) integrated with the Bidadari Community Club, a neighbourhood police centre, the Woodleigh Village Hawker Centre and Woodleigh MRT — nature-inspired gathering spaces knit into the adjacent Bidadari Park and Alkaff Lake.

sights.address: Kallang Park Connector (through Potong Pasir), Singapore
sights.w: Potong Pasir means 'cut sand' in Malay — from 1910-1937 the area was sand quarries whose worked-out pits became ponds linked to the Kallang River. The river still threads the estate, and the Bidadari/Kallang Park Connector now runs alongside it, joining Potong Pasir to Bishan-Ang Mo Kio Park and down to the Kallang basin.

sights.address: MacPherson Road (Aljunied to Paya Lebar), Singapore
sights.w: MacPherson takes its name from Colonel Ronald MacPherson, the Straits Settlements' first Colonial Secretary; MacPherson Road itself was once Jalan Klapa, running through coconut plantations. The estate's first eleven 10-storey blocks went up in 1961, an early chapter of Singapore high-rise housing, beside the Circuit Road town and the Tai Seng/Paya Lebar industrial belt.

One of the rare central estates with no mega-mall or high-rise sprawl, Potong Pasir keeps a laid-back, almost kampong-spirited feel between Toa Payoh and Sennett. The sign-crowned Block 142 at the foot of the sloping-roof blocks is its unofficial gateway and most-photographed civic landmark.
sights.k: Public estate; view from ground level
